meta.disclaimer: General guidance, not legal advice. Rules change and local closures apply: confirm with the office before you collect.
meta.how_read: Each source names the date it was read and how: 'fetcher' (the build tool's web reader), 'curl' (a direct download from the build machine, used where the site refused the web reader), or 'unverified' (the page refused every attempt; the rule says so and states nothing from it).

BLM.title: BLM public land (Bureau of Land Management)
BLM.who: The BLM field office manages the surface and, where the mineral estate is federal, the minerals.
allowed: Reasonable amounts of rocks, mineral specimens, semiprecious gemstones and common invertebrate fossils for personal, noncommercial use, without a permit or fee, outside developed recreation sites and where not posted closed (43 CFR 8365.1-5(b); BLM rockhounding page).
Hand tools, gold pans and metal detectors; the BLM Montana guide says power equipment and explosives may not be used except for woodcutting and certain dredging.
Petrified wood: up to 25 pounds plus one piece per day and 250 pounds per calendar year, no pooling, personal use only (43 CFR 3622.4).

Arizona BLM states its 'reasonable' limit as 25 pounds per day and 250 pounds per year for mineral specimens, common invertebrate fossils, gemstones, rock and petrified wood; other state offices publish their own figures.
not_allowed: Selling or bartering what you collect (a permit or contract is needed for commercial collection, 43 CFR 8365.1-5(c)).
Developed recreation sites, areas posted closed, and land where the mineral estate is privately owned.
Minerals on an active mining claim without the claimant's permission.
Vertebrate fossils, uncommon invertebrate or plant fossils (permit only); artifacts, arrowheads, historic objects and sites; cave resources.
Wilderness and wilderness study areas: only hobby collecting without surface disturbance (BLM Montana guide); more restrictive rules in ACECs, national monuments and landmarks: ask first.
BLM.ask: The local BLM field office (it can tell you if a spot is public land and whether a claim or closure applies).

43 CFR 3622.4 Petrified wood collection rules

USFS.title: National Forest or Grassland (US Forest Service)
USFS.who: The ranger district. Forest Service policy allows rockhounding for personal, hobby and noncommercial use; most national forest land is open to it.
allowed: Rocks, semiprecious stones and mineral specimens for personal, hobby, noncommercial use. The Forest Service provides for this 'through a free use permit' (FS-1091); Region 4 says the permit is free and allows small amounts for personal use. Many districts treat small hand collection as needing no paperwork: ask the district.
Low-impact activity with little surface disturbance (hand collection, gold panning, metal detecting) generally needs no plan of operations.

Common invertebrate and plant fossils: casual collecting without a permit where the land is not closed, up to 25 pounds a day and 100 pounds a calendar year, hand tools, negligible disturbance (36 CFR 291.5, 291.11).
Petrified wood in limited quantities for personal use under a free-use permit; free-use areas may be designated (36 CFR 228.62(e)).
not_allowed: Selling or bartering specimens collected for hobby use; fossils collected casually cannot be sold.
Mechanical equipment, blasting; collection that conflicts with existing mineral permits, leases, claims or sales.
Artifacts and archaeological resources (36 CFR 261.9); meteorites.

National monuments, wilderness and other special areas: collecting may or may not be allowed, check with the district. East of the Mississippi, check in with the district before rockhounding or prospecting.
USFS.ask: The local ranger district office (free-use permit, closures, district rules).

sources.title: USDA Forest Service: Rockhounding Guide FS-1091 (June 2017)

36 CFR 291.5 Definitions (casual collecting, reasonable amount) (LII copy)
36 CFR 291.11 Casual collecting on National Forest System lands (LII copy)
Forest Service Region 4: Rock and mineral collecting

NPS.title: National Park System unit (National Park Service)
NPS.who: The park superintendent. The Organic Act directs the NPS to conserve all park resources, rocks and minerals included.
allowed: Nothing in general. Narrow exceptions exist in a few units (some Alaska parks under 36 CFR 13.35; limited gold panning at Whiskeytown under 36 CFR 7.91; catlinite at Pipestone for American Indians).
not_allowed: Possessing, destroying, removing, digging or disturbing mineral resources, fossilized or nonfossilized paleontological specimens, cultural or archeological resources, cave formations, plants and wildlife (36 CFR 2.1(a)(1)).
NPS.ask: The park (superintendent's office) or the NPS Geologic Resources Division.

sources.title: 36 CFR 2.1 Preservation of natural, cultural and archeological resources (LII copy)
NPS: Recreational collection of rocks and minerals, legal instruments

FWS.title: National Wildlife Refuge (US Fish and Wildlife Service)
allowed: Nothing unless the refuge authorizes it.
not_allowed: Destruction, injury, defacement, disturbance or unauthorized removal of any public property, including natural objects, on or from any national wildlife refuge (50 CFR 27.61).
Casual fossil collecting under the Paleontological Resources Preservation Act applies only to BLM, Reclamation and Forest Service land, not refuges.

sources.title: 50 CFR 27.61 Destruction or removal of property (LII copy)
16 U.S.C. 470aaa-3 Casual collecting exception (LII)

BOR.title: Bureau of Reclamation land
BOR.who: The Reclamation area office (and often a managing partner around reservoirs).
allowed: Casual collecting of common invertebrate and plant fossils without a permit, up to 25 pounds per day per person, hand tools, negligible disturbance (43 CFR 49.810; 16 U.S.C. 470aaa-3).
not_allowed: Vertebrate fossils without a permit; sale of fossils.
Rocks and minerals: no general Reclamation rule was found when this file was built. The Utah Geological Survey lists dam sites among lands where collecting is prohibited.
BOR.ask: The Reclamation area office or the agency that manages recreation there.
BOR.note: Rock and mineral collecting on Reclamation land has no source on file: treat it as closed until the office says otherwise.

sources.title: 43 CFR 49.810 Casual collecting (LII copy)
Utah Geological Survey PI-62a: Rockhound guide, land ownership

DOD.title: Military land (Department of Defense, Army Corps of Engineers)
DOD.who: The installation or the Corps district.
not_allowed: Entering and collecting on military reservations: 'both illegal and dangerous' (Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology); 'strictly prohibited' (Utah Geological Survey). Corps of Engineers project land has its own rules: ask the project office.
DOD.ask: The installation's public affairs office or the Corps project office.

sources.title: Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology: Rocks and Minerals (collecting)

TRIBAL.title: Tribal land (reservations, Bureau of Indian Affairs trust land)
allowed: Only with the tribe's permission.
not_allowed: Trespassing and collecting on reservations without permission from the tribal authorities (Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology); collecting is 'strictly prohibited' on tribal lands (Utah Geological Survey).
TRIBAL.ask: The tribe's natural resources or land office.

sources.title: Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology: Rocks and Minerals (collecting)
Utah Geological Survey PI-62a: Rockhound guide, land ownership

OTHER_FED.title: Other federal land (DOE, NRCS, USDA research, other agencies)
OTHER_FED.who: The agency named on the map (for example the Department of Energy at Oak Ridge).
OTHER_FED.note: No general collecting rule on file for this agency. Treat the land as closed to collecting until the office says otherwise.

TVA.title: TVA public land (Tennessee Valley Authority)
TVA.who: TVA Natural Resources (reservoir lands and shoreline).
TVA.ask: TVA, through its Rules for Use of TVA Public Lands page and its public land information line.
TVA.note: TVA publishes 'Rules for Use of TVA Public Lands'. The page refused automated reading when this file was built (HTTP 403 on 2026-10-24), so no rule is stated here. Read it before collecting on TVA land; it is the authority for artifacts, metal detectors and natural materials on TVA land.

sources.title: TVA: Rules for Use of TVA Public Lands

STATE_TRUST_AZ.title: Arizona State Trust Land
allowed: Being on trust land at all needs an ASLD Recreational Use Permit (camping, hiking, travel), per the BLM Arizona pamphlet.
not_allowed: Rockhounding and metal detecting on Arizona State Trust Land (BLM Arizona pamphlet: 'Rockhounding and metal detecting are not allowed on Arizona State Trust Land').
STATE_TRUST_AZ.note: The ASLD permit terms page refused automated reading (403), so the statement comes from the BLM Arizona pamphlet.

sources.title: BLM Arizona: Rock Hounding in Arizona (BLM/AZ/GI-14/009)
ASLD: Recreational permit terms and conditions

STATE_TRUST_UT.title: Utah trust land (SITLA)
STATE_TRUST_UT.who: School and Institutional Trust Lands Administration (SITLA).
allowed: Rockhounding with SITLA's annual rockhounding permit (a fee is charged): up to 25 pounds plus one piece per person per day, 250 pounds per year, hand collection.
Lands of the Division of Forestry, Fire and State Lands: with the Division's permission (UGS PI-62a).
not_allowed: Collecting without the permit (trespass); commercial collection.
Land under an active mineral lease or active mining without the lessee's permission; land posted closed.
Other state agencies' land: state parks, sovereign lands, Division of Wildlife Resources and Department of Transportation land (collecting prohibited).
Vertebrate fossils, dinosaur tracks and artifacts (never without a permit, on state and federal land).
STATE_TRUST_UT.ask: SITLA (permit) and the Utah Geological Survey's collecting-rules page.
STATE_TRUST_UT.note: SITLA's own pages refused automated reading (403); the rule is taken from the Utah Geological Survey, a state agency.

sources.title: Utah Geological Survey: Rock, Mineral and Fossil Collecting Rules
Utah Geological Survey PI-62a: Rockhound guide, land ownership
SITLA rockhounding permit form

STATE_TRUST_NV.title: Nevada state land
STATE_TRUST_NV.who: Nevada Division of State Lands (very little trust land remains in state ownership).
not_allowed: Nevada state parks: hobby collecting is not allowed (Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology).
STATE_TRUST_NV.ask: Nevada Division of State Lands for state-owned parcels; the Nevada Division of Minerals for land status and claims.
STATE_TRUST_NV.note: No Division of State Lands collecting rule was found when this file was built. The NBMG page gives Nevada's general picture: hobby collecting on most public land except state and federal parks, recreation areas, wildlife refuges and wilderness; minerals on a valid claim belong to the claimant.

sources.title: Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology: Rocks and Minerals (collecting)

STATE_TRUST_NM.title: New Mexico state trust land
allowed: Recreational access (hiking, sightseeing, picnicking, wildlife watching, photography) with a Recreational Access Permit or other written authorization from the Commissioner (19.2.19.9 NMAC).
not_allowed: Mineral exploration, development or mining, or collecting valuable rocks or minerals (19.2.19.18(A)(15) NMAC).
Disturbing or removing historical, archaeological, paleontological or cultural sites or artifacts (19.2.19.18(A)(3)).
Land under a business lease, or with oil and gas or mining operations, is not open to recreational access.
STATE_TRUST_NM.ask: New Mexico State Land Office (permit) for anything beyond recreational access.

sources.title: 19.2.19 NMAC Recreational access to state trust lands

STATE_TRUST_CO.title: Colorado state trust land
allowed: Access only where a parcel is leased for public recreation (Colorado Parks and Wildlife access program) and only the uses that lease allows.
not_allowed: Entering trust land in general: 'This land, called trust land, is not open to the public.' (State Land Board). No collecting rule is published; collecting is not among the allowed uses.
STATE_TRUST_CO.ask: Colorado State Land Board, or Colorado Parks and Wildlife for a leased parcel's rules.

sources.title: Colorado State Land Board: Public access on trust land

STATE_TRUST_WY.title: Wyoming state trust land
STATE_TRUST_WY.who: Office of State Lands and Investments (OSLI), Board of Land Commissioners Chapter 13 rules.
allowed: Hunting, fishing and general recreational use of legally accessible trust land (Chapter 13, since 1988).
not_allowed: Off-road vehicle use, overnight camping, open fires; anything that damages the land, roads, improvements or a lessee's property; cultivated cropland.
Any use outside Chapter 13 needs a temporary use permit or special use lease. The FAQ does not address rock collecting: assume it needs OSLI's authorization.
STATE_TRUST_WY.note: OSLI's FAQ does not mention collecting rocks, minerals or fossils; the rule above is what it does say.

sources.title: Wyoming OSLI: Frequently asked questions (state trust land use)

STATE_TRUST_OR.title: Oregon state land
STATE_TRUST_OR.who: Department of State Lands (DSL) for state-owned uplands; Oregon Parks and Recreation for the ocean shore.
allowed: ORS 273.715 directs DSL to make rules for semiprecious stones and petrified wood on state land that allow free noncommercial collection of reasonable quantities; a permit is needed for commercial removal or removal worth $500 or more.

Ocean shore: a small quantity of agates and other rocks, shells and fossils for personal use, at most a one-gallon container per person per day and three gallons per year, individual containers; hand-operated tools only (OAR 736-021-0090).
not_allowed: Digging up or removing sand, soil, rock, historical or fossil material on the ocean shore beyond the personal-use exception without written permission.
Motorized equipment for prospecting on the ocean shore.
STATE_TRUST_OR.ask: DSL for a state-owned upland parcel (the DSL rules themselves were not found online when this file was built); the state park office for the shore.

sources.title: ORS 273.715 Rules for removal of semiprecious stones and petrified wood (oregon.public.law)
OAR 736-021-0090 Cultural, historic, natural and wildlife resources on the ocean shore (LII copy)

STATE_TRUST_ID.title: Idaho endowment land
allowed: Public recreation on legally accessible endowment land where it does not degrade the land, interfere with management or harm returns to the beneficiaries (Land Board policy; IDAPA 20.05.01).
not_allowed: Collecting valuable rocks or minerals without separate authorization from IDL (IDL recreation policy page: 'collecting valuable rocks or minerals require separate authorization from IDL').

sources.title: Idaho Department of Lands: Recreation policy on endowment land
IDAPA 20.05.01 Rules pertaining to the recreational use of endowment land

STATE_TRUST_CA.title: California state school land
STATE_TRUST_CA.who: California State Lands Commission (about 460,000 acres remain, mostly in the desert).
STATE_TRUST_CA.note: No State Lands Commission collecting rule was found when this file was built. State parks have their own rule (see the California state park entry).

STATE_PARK_TN.title: Tennessee state park or state natural area
STATE_PARK_TN.who: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation, Division of State Parks.
allowed: State parks: gathering small quantities of pebbles or small rocks by hand for personal use (Rule 0400-02-02-.18(4)).
not_allowed: Collecting rocks for commercial sale or use; intentional destruction, defacement or removal of any natural feature or non-renewable natural resource without a scientific permit (0400-02-02-.18(1)).
Mineral or metal detectors (0400-02-02-.18(6)).
State natural areas: no removal of any natural material, product or object; a collecting permit is required for collecting in all areas (0400-02-08-.21).
STATE_PARK_TN.ask: The park office; the Division of State Parks for a scientific collecting permit.

sources.title: Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0400-02-02 Public use and recreation (Division of State Parks)
Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0400-02-08 Management of Tennessee natural resource areas

STATE_PARK_CA.title: California state park unit
STATE_PARK_CA.who: California Department of Parks and Recreation.
allowed: Rockhounding only in units or portions posted open for it: at most 15 pounds of mineralogical material (or one specimen plus 15 pounds) per person per day per unit; in state recreation areas only beaches, wave-action zones and flood-prone gravel bars (14 CCR 4611).
Gold panning counts as rockhounding; a gold pan is the only tool allowed.
not_allowed: Destroying, disturbing or removing earth, sand, gravel, minerals, rocks, paleontological features or cave features anywhere else (14 CCR 4307).
Tools other than gold pans; selling or commercial use; arrowheads, stone tools and other archaeological specimens.
STATE_PARK_CA.ask: The park unit (district orders can close units to rockhounding).

sources.title: 14 CCR 4307 Geological features (LII copy)
14 CCR 4611 Rockhounding (LII copy)

STATE_PARK.title: State park (general)
not_allowed: Collecting is prohibited in state parks in the states whose guidance was read (Utah, Nevada); Tennessee allows only small quantities of pebbles by hand and California only in posted units. Expect a prohibition unless the park says otherwise.

sources.title: Utah Geological Survey PI-62a: Rockhound guide, land ownership
Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology: Rocks and Minerals (collecting)

STATE.title: Other state land (wildlife areas, state forests, trust land in a state not listed)
STATE.who: The state agency named on the map (for example the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency for a WMA).
STATE.ask: That agency's regional office. Choose a state below to see its trust-land rule if it is on file.
STATE.note: No rule on file for this agency: treat the land as closed to collecting until the office says otherwise.

LOCAL.title: City, county or regional land
LOCAL.who: The city or county parks department or the district that owns it.
LOCAL.note: No general rule on file; local parks commonly prohibit removing natural materials. Ask first.

NGO.title: Private conservation land (land trust, nature conservancy)
not_allowed: Collecting without the owner's permission: private land rules apply.

sources.title: Utah Geological Survey PI-62a: private lands (owner's permission)

PRIVATE.title: Private land
PRIVATE.who: The landowner (the county register of deeds or assessor's parcel map names the owner).
allowed: Collecting only with the owner's permission, on the owner's terms.
not_allowed: Entering or collecting without permission: 'On private land or land encumbered by mining claims, the collector must get the permission of the owner before removing any rocks or minerals' (Utah Geological Survey); 'One should always contact the owner before collecting on private property' (Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology); 'Respect private property rights, and do not trespass' (Forest Service FS-1091).
PRIVATE.ask: The owner. In Tennessee, criminal trespass is Tenn. Code 39-14-405 (its text could not be read automatically when this file was built).

sources.title: Utah Geological Survey PI-62a: Rockhound guide, land ownership
Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology: Rocks and Minerals (collecting)
USDA Forest Service: Rockhounding Guide FS-1091
Tenn. Code 39-14-405 Criminal trespass (Justia)

UNKNOWN.title: No managed-area record here
UNKNOWN.who: Most likely a private owner; sometimes a gap in the data.
allowed: Collecting only with the owner's permission.
not_allowed: Assuming land with no record is public.
UNKNOWN.ask: The county parcel map for the owner; a county parcel service can be added under Layers > Add a layer by URL.

sources.title: Utah Geological Survey PI-62a: private lands (owner's permission)

CLAIM_ACTIVE.title: Active mining claim on this spot
CLAIM_ACTIVE.who: The claimant holds the right to develop and extract the locatable minerals (gold, silver, gemstones, most hard-rock minerals). The surface stays public land under the surface agency's rules.
allowed: Being on the surface for recreation under the surface agency's rules: a mining claim 'does not include exclusive surface rights' (BLM).
not_allowed: Collecting minerals on the claim without the claimant's permission: 'Minerals found on mining claims belong to the claim holder and may not be collected without the claimant's permission' (BLM Montana guide); BLM's rockhounding page lists active mining claims among the places collection is generally not allowed.
Metal detecting for precious metals on a claim without the claimant's permission (Forest Service FS-1091).
CLAIM_ACTIVE.ask: The claimant: look the serial number up in BLM's Mineral and Land Records System (MLRS) for the name and address.

sources.title: BLM: Mining claims (locatable minerals)
BLM Montana: Can I Keep This? (rev. 2021)
BLM: Rockhounding on Public Lands
BLM Mineral and Land Records System (claimant lookup)

CLAIM_CLOSED.title: Claim closed within the past year
CLAIM_CLOSED.who: BLM's record shows a claim here whose case closed in the past year; claims are mapped by legal description to the quarter section, so the outline is approximate.
allowed: If the claim is truly closed, the land's own rules apply (see the manager's entry above).
not_allowed: Treating the closure as certain: the record can lag, a new claim can be staked on the same ground, and an adjoining active claim may overlap. Check MLRS.
CLAIM_CLOSED.ask: BLM MLRS for the case status; the BLM field office.

sources.title: BLM MLRS Mining Claims - Closed (past year) feature service description

FOSSILS_FEDERAL.title: Fossils on BLM, Forest Service and Reclamation land (Paleontological Resources Preservation Act)
FOSSILS_FEDERAL.who: The surface agency, under 16 U.S.C. 470aaa and its regulations.
allowed: Casual collecting of a reasonable amount of common invertebrate and plant fossils for noncommercial personal use, by surface collection or non-powered hand tools, with negligible disturbance, where the land is open to it.
BLM and Reclamation: at most 25 pounds per day per person (43 CFR 49.810). Forest Service: at most 25 pounds per day and 100 pounds per calendar year (36 CFR 291.5).
not_allowed: Vertebrate fossils (dinosaurs, mammals, fish, reptiles), and invertebrate or plant fossils the agency has determined are not common: permit only.
Selling fossils collected casually; collecting in National Park System units and wildlife refuges (not covered by the casual-collecting exception).
FOSSILS_FEDERAL.ask: The field office or ranger district (local limits, closures and which fossils count as common).

WILDERNESS.title: Wilderness or wilderness study area
WILDERNESS.who: The surface agency (BLM or Forest Service) under its wilderness rules.
allowed: BLM: 'Only hobby collecting is allowed in wilderness and wilderness study areas and must not involve surface disturbance' (BLM Montana guide; the Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology says the same).
not_allowed: Any surface disturbance; motorized or mechanized equipment.
Forest Service wilderness: collecting 'may or may not be allowed' (FS-1091): ask the ranger district first.
WILDERNESS.ask: The field office or ranger district for the wilderness unit.
